decisions.reason: Connects the session/tool worker to the host installation npm is replacing, explains the host dies at remove/linkStuff so no tool result can be recorded, and treats it as a structural self-host hazard while preserving the unknown final tool outcome.

Explains env-state.txt: package content present but dsh/dsh.cmd missing and dsh.ps1 stale, so content presence does not prove a complete install; relates the manually swapped tree to broken shims and rejects hand-repair.

Grounds the remedy in repair-notes.md: rerun npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.2-rc.1 from outside the stopped host so npm regenerates shims, verify rc.1, align the source checkout to the tag; keeps recorded repair separate from proposed verification.

Requires the agent to recognize it runs on the upgrade target and hand off: fully stop the host first, exact-version pinned install from a genuinely external context, restart, refresh, verify; distinguishes existing stop/pin rules from the new refuse-inside-the-target rule.

Describes a self-mutation guard comparing the install target with its own runtime/worker paths; uses the version-only alpha.5→rc.1 diff to skip plugin migration; checks shims, version markers and real plugin loading, with backup cleanup only after verification.

caps.reason: Final plan explicitly refuses to execute the upgrade from inside the target host and requires a fully stopped host plus external execution.
Manual directory swaps and handmade shims are explicitly rejected in favor of the formal external pinned reinstall.
